entities.summary:
The Sweden Democrats, founded on February 6, 1988, in Stockholm, have emerged as a notable political force in Sweden, representing a shift in the country's political landscape towards right-wing populism. This party's significance lies in its ability to influence national debates regarding immigration, identity, and cultural integration, reflecting broader trends in Europe that have seen similar parties gaining traction. Key figures in its history include Jimmie Åkesson, who has served as the party leader since 2005, guiding its transition from a fringe party to a major player in Swedish politics.

The journey of the Sweden Democrats is marked by their early years, where they struggled to shed their connections to various extremist factions, to their breakthrough in the 2010 elections, where they secured seats in the Swedish Parliament (Riksdag) for the first time with 5.7% of the vote. This pivotal moment catalyzed their growth, leading to increased support in subsequent elections, including 17.5% in 2018, thereby forcing traditional parties to reconsider their strategies and coalitions. The party's rise has been fueled by a growing discontent with the status quo regarding immigration policies and social integration, echoing sentiments seen across Europe, particularly in the wake of the 2015 migrant crisis.

The legacy of the Sweden Democrats is characterized by their impact on Swedish politics and public discourse, as they have compelled other parties to address issues of nationalism and immigration more openly. They have transformed the political dialogue around these topics, influencing public policies and shaping voter sentiment. This shift can be seen as part of a larger trend across Europe where populist movements are reshaping the political landscape, leading to increased polarization and debate over national identity and governance.
